description:
After Rick Rubin and Kanye West cut down Yeezus to the final ten tracks, Kanye still saw potential in much of the cut material. Thus, shortly after Yeezus was released, an EP of leftovers titled Lost Yeezus was already being teased. The project then evolved into a full-fledged album of mostly new material, with Yeezus 2 acting as a codename before they could choose the last name. This project would develop into So Help Me God as the songs evolved.

(06/18/2013) (Yeezus officially releases)
(07/16/2014) (Kanye begins hosting recording sessions while staying in Mexico)

title: Ant Clemons - Pootie Tang [V1]
status_source_term: OG File | OG File | CD Quality
description: Solo Ant Clemons version. According to xtcy, the file was in a folder of Jeremih and Ant Clemons tracks. On February 10th, 2018, Legion on Instagram posted a snippet along with what looks to be a scrapped music video. According to Ant Clemons in a Rolling Stone article, "the first day [Bongo ByTheWay and I] met we did 11 records... There’s a couch in the studio, so if I outwork Bongo and he falls asleep, I can sleep on his couch.'". The article later states "Bongo stayed awake for long enough to be impressed with Clemons’ output. He took Clemons to meet Jeremih; West called on Jeremih to come to Wyoming to participate in the sessions for Ye, Jeremih played West a demo with Clemons titled 'All Mine'. and West pounced on it". According to Ant Clemons, the song was shown to Ye one week before the album's release. ROBOTSCOTT's release credit likely comes out of courtesy for him being a large contributor to this version of the song and shaping the vision, as none of this production is on release and the stems do not mention him at all.
